algorithm: value = round(12000 * exp(-0.0085 * (rank-1)) / rank**0.13). 1QB multiplies QB value by 0.38. Picks map to equivalent ranks on that curve.

players.name: Josh Allen
notes: The Keep #1 · average 2.64 across 40 Superflex boards
plus: Seven-board Superflex lock: Keep #1, average 2.0.
Dual-threat floor still separates him from every other aging QB1.
minus: Turns 31 in 2026 - first real dynasty age tax on a perennial 1.01.
Yates PPR has him in the late 20s; 1QB redraft does not pay the SF premium.
grafs: Josh Allen is still the player Ball Keep is built around. Seven sources - PFN, Dynasty Nerds, FantasyPros, KeepTradeCut, and the three X experts we track - all have him inside the top four Superflex assets, and the average lands at 2.0. That is not a recency spike. It is the market admitting that a quarterback who runs, extends, and finishes in the end zone is the safest way to keep a Superflex roster relevant through 2029.

The 2025 tape is the same argument on film: launch-point throws and designed keepers, with the Bills still built to let him create when protection breaks. Redraft boards (Field Yates has him in the high 20s) treat him as a mid QB1 because 1QB leagues do not have to pay the second-starter tax. Dynasty Superflex does. That split is the whole point of The Keep.

The minus is honest: he will be 31 this season, and the first time a 23-year-old passer (Maye) outranks him on a short list, the age conversation gets louder. We are not selling the 1.01 for that. We are naming it. If you are rebuilding past 2028, Maye is the bet. If you are trying to win the next two title windows, Allen is still the chip you do not put in a trade calculator for fun.

The 2025 Can't-Miss play - 63 yards of broken tackles - is the scouting report: speed, strength, and a refusal to be brought down by the first or second man.

Where boards disagree is not talent, it is format. Erickson sliding him to eight is a Superflex tell: some experts will take Daniels/Herbert before they take a receiver. The minus is Cincinnati's quarterback room, not Chase. If Burrow misses time, the weekly floor dips and the 'is this still a WR1 week?' tweets start. Dynasty can live through that. grafs: Jonathan Taylor is the reddest redraft name on a dynasty site. Yates has him seventh in PPR. Our standard board has him fourth because that is what 20-carry touchdown backs do in non-PPR. The Colts 2025 reel is Taylor as a hammer: inside, outside, enough burst left to finish.

The Keep at 31 is not a smear. It is Superflex math. Quarterbacks and young skill players eat the first two rounds, and a running back with Taylor's injury history does not get the Gibbs/Bijan premium. You can win a 2026 redraft title with Taylor as your RB1. You cannot build a 2029 roster around him as your only expensive back.

If a dynasty manager still has Taylor ranked like 2021, buy the rest of their team. If a redraft manager is letting him slide because of 'the injury,' take him and stop overthinking. Format is the ranking.

Market: £4.0m, 2 boards on the file. Price is the FPL tax, not the rank. The Premier is who produced and who the boards still believe. FPL's own EP-next is 1.0. ICT 6.2.

Instruction: he is on the 400, which is already a statement, and he is not a star. Stash in Sleeper if the minutes are real. Do not let a Pitch screenshot make you start him over a Premier top-80. Nearby on The Premier: Rio Cardines, Julio Soler Barreto. Versus The Pitch (Sleeper-only #404), the hybrid moves him down to #405. That move is the third list doing its job.

Age 20 is the other half of a hybrid. The 2025/26 counting line is one season. The Athletic-style youth lean on this board exists specifically so a Spurs kid does not get stuck behind a 32-year-old who had a nice bonus year. Sleeper still has to see the minutes. 2 starts is the beginning of a case, not the end of one.

Full-backs and centre-backs separate on this board by attacking events. 0 goals and 0 assists are how a defender outruns his GA column. Without those, you are betting 0 clean sheets and the CBI stream (6) against 3 goals against at −2 a piece. Spurs's 2026/27 defensive shape is therefore half of this player's rank. The other half already happened, across 2 starts.

How to use the file: The Pitch is the Sleeper-only 400 (he is #404 there). The Premier is the 50/50 with every other board we track. Attack, Midfield, Defence, and Keepers re-rank the same Sleeper table by position.
